clue.text: Female college student without work in confinement

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the student's letters sit around the work

parts.note: a co-ed is a female student at a mixed college
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A woman at university is stuck indoors with nothing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking', but here it means outside, wrapping the student round the work.
explanation.definitionFit: Cooped up means shut in a small space, like a hen kept in its coop, so confined.

clue.text: Chore, mixing this pigment

indicators.note: mixing stirs the letters of the household task together into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Mixing paint is presented as a dull household job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This pigment' makes the clue's own wordplay the thing being mixed, a light self-referential touch.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is an earthy yellow-brown colouring material made from clay and iron oxide.

clue.text: Straight-laced girl in Carthaginian setting

indicators.note: in places the girl inside the word for Carthaginian, which closes round her
a setting holds something within it, as a ring's mount holds a stone, so this word encloses the girl

parts.note: Punic is the adjective for ancient Carthage and its people
a girl's name

explanation.surface: A prim young woman is pictured in an ancient North African backdrop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setting' is the frame word: Punic surrounds the girl, as a jewel setting holds a stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Puritanical behaviour is strict and prudish in moral matters, which is what strait-laced describes.

clue.text: Dredge river enclosure

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland
a pen is an enclosure for animals

explanation.surface: Someone is dredging the muddy bed of a river by a fenced area.
explanation.definitionFit: To dredge a channel is to scoop out its bottom so it becomes deeper; the verbs match.

clue.text: It's brought up from the rear with spirit

definitions.text: It's brought up from the rear with spirit

parts.note: surface reading: something hauled forward from behind, perhaps reinforcements to an army's back line
setter's reading: a small container of whisky or brandy carried in a back trouser pocket and pulled out

explanation.surface: Troops are brought up from the rear with fighting spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: Spirit sounds like morale, but it is liquor; the rear is the drinker's backside, where a back pocket sits.
explanation.definitionFit: This small flat bottle for liquor is designed to sit in a pocket near the hip.

clue.text: Play bringing agony to theatre

parts.note: heartbreak is overwhelming grief
a theatre is called a house, as in 'full house'

explanation.surface: A stage drama brings anguish to the auditorium.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a 1919 comedy by George Bernard Shaw.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaw's drama of that title is a stage work, so it is a specific example of a play.

clue.text: Soldier climbing gets into deeper trouble in descent

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means the soldier's letters run upward, bottom to top
gets into means the soldier enters the other word and is surrounded by it
trouble disturbs the following word so its letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
GI is an American private soldier

explanation.surface: A climber on a rock face gets into deeper trouble while coming back down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climbing' and 'descent' look like a mountaineering story; descent is the definition, meaning ancestry.
explanation.definitionFit: Descent in the sense of lineage or ancestry is a person's or animal's recorded line of forebears.

clue.text: Gaol a thief carrying this weapon

indicators.note: carrying means the words ahead hold the answer within them, across a word break

parts.note: the letters run from the end of the first word through the second into the third

explanation.surface: A prison holds a robber who was armed.
explanation.walkthrough: A lathi is a long iron-bound bamboo stick, used especially by police in India.
explanation.definitionFit: The lathi is a heavy club or staff carried as a weapon in South Asia.

clue.text: It enables one to get well away

definitions.text: It enables one to get well away

parts.note: surface reading: escape cleanly, make a good getaway

parts.words: It enables one to get well
parts.note: setter's reading: time off work granted so an ill employee can recover at home

explanation.walkthrough: 'Get well away' reads as a clean escape, but splits into recovering while away from the workplace.
explanation.definitionFit: Absence permitted by an employer for illness lets the worker recuperate away from their job.

clue.text: He directs men to load some bananas

parts.note: to charge a gun or battery is to load it
a hand is a cluster of bananas on the stem

explanation.surface: A foreman orders his workers to stack up the fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: A chargehand is a British term for a worker in charge of a small team, below a foreman.
explanation.definitionFit: This supervisor leads a gang of workmen, giving them their instructions on site.

clue.text: Pinch food

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a fold gathered and stitched in cloth
second meaning: British slang for snacks and sweets, especially at boarding school

explanation.walkthrough: Pinch tempts as 'steal'; it is the dressmaker's sense, a gathered fold.
explanation.definitionFit: A tuck is a pinched-in fold sewn into fabric, and in British school slang tuck means sweets and snacks.

clue.text: Safety device testable in crash

indicators.note: a crash smashes things up, so the letters before it come out jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A piece of safety equipment is put to the test in a collision.
explanation.definitionFit: The strap across a car passenger restrains them in a collision, protecting them from injury.

clue.text: Sounds like pump is grating

indicators.note: sounds like tells us the answer is spoken the same as a synonym of the following word

parts.note: to pump someone for information is to question them hard, to grill them

explanation.surface: A water pump is making a harsh scraping noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grating' wants to be the noise; it is the noun, a metal lattice.
explanation.definitionFit: A grille is a framework of metal bars over a window or opening, which is a grating.

clue.text: First in supermarket to take tin to check out

indicators.note: first in asks for only the opening letter of the shop word that follows

parts.note: the opening letter of supermarket
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A shopper picks up a tin first thing and heads for the checkout.
explanation.walkthrough: The supermarket scene fits: tins get passed over a scanner at the till.
explanation.definitionFit: To scan something is to look it over closely, which is to examine or check it out.

clue.text: Songbird has easy task keeping loud note up

indicators.note: keeping means the easy task holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: a cinch is something very easy

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the pair of letters for loud and the note are read bottom to top

parts.note: f is forte, the musical direction for loud
fah is the fourth note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A singing bird finds it easy to hold a loud note.
explanation.definitionFit: The chaffinch is a common European finch known for its cheerful song, so a songbird.

clue.text: It controls resistance that rose after reform

indicators.note: reform reshapes the preceding words, so their letters are put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Political opposition grew after a reform programme was introduced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resistance' reads as political opposition; here it is electrical resistance.
explanation.definitionFit: A rheostat is a variable resistor used to adjust current in a circuit, as in a light dimmer.

clue.text: New town still in development period

indicators.note: in puts the word for still inside the period word

parts.note: a stage is a period in a process of development
even and still both intensify, as in 'still better' and 'even better'

explanation.surface: A newly built town is still being developed.
explanation.walkthrough: Stevenage in Hertfordshire was the first of Britain's post-war planned new towns.
explanation.definitionFit: Stevenage was designated in 1946 as one of the planned new towns built to rehouse Londoners.

clue.text: Figure of speech encountered previously in saying

parts.note: to have encountered someone is to have met them

indicators.note: in saying means the words are spoken aloud, so we go by their sound not spelling

parts.note: afore is an old or dialect word for before, previously

explanation.surface: A turn of phrase has been heard before in a proverb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saying' looks like a noun for a proverb, but it is the sound signal: met afore, said out loud.
explanation.definitionFit: A metaphor is a figure of speech that describes something as being another thing.

clue.text: Little women with a noble lady in Italy

parts.note: Little Women is Louisa May Alcott's novel about the four March sisters, collectively the Marches
taken as written

explanation.surface: Small girls are accompanied by an Italian aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little women' looks like small females, but it is the book title, whose heroines share the surname March.
explanation.definitionFit: A marchesa is the wife or widow of an Italian marquis, or a marchioness in her own right.

clue.text: Prime Minister's original home

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Anthony, British premier from 1955 to 1957
second meaning: the biblical garden where Adam and Eve first lived

explanation.surface: A premier returns to the house where he started out.
explanation.walkthrough: The ''s' is short for 'is', joining the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Anthony was Churchill's successor as premier, and Genesis places humanity's first dwelling in that garden.

clue.text: Quarters invaded by very odd creature up in arms

indicators.note: invaded by means the quarters have the other letters forced into their middle

parts.note: west and north, two of the compass quarters

indicators.note: odd means strange, so the letters of the word before it appear in a strange order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Living quarters are overrun by a bizarre beast that is furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up in arms' means angry, but here it means displayed on a coat of arms; 'odd' looks like 'very strange'.
explanation.definitionFit: A wyvern is a two-legged winged dragon that appears as a charge in heraldry.

clue.text: Continent's the source of critical article on a French individual

parts.note: taken as written
Fr is the abbreviation for French
I is the single individual, the first person

indicators.note: a source is where something begins, so only the opening letter is taken

parts.note: the opening letter of critical
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A disparaging essay about a Frenchman provokes a quarrel across a continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' means placed after: the source and article come after a French individual.
explanation.definitionFit: Africa is the second largest of the world's continents.

clue.text: One mark produced on line from blue dye

indicators.note: line from the colour word means the letter for line is taken away from it

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
M is the abbreviation for the German mark
taken as written
L is a common abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A stain left on a washing line by a blue colourant.
explanation.definitionFit: To imbue something is to saturate or stain it with colour, which is to dye it.

clue.text: Play that could make one weep

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a pollen allergy that brings on watery eyes

explanation.walkthrough: Weeping suggests a tragedy, but Coward's play is a comedy; the tears are from pollen.
explanation.definitionFit: Coward wrote the comedy of that name, and the allergy to grass pollen causes streaming eyes and sneezing.

clue.text: Praise enthusiastically, without giving many a rise

parts.note: ex is Latin for out of or without, as in ex dividend

indicators.note: in a down entry, a rise means the word for many is read upward, bottom to top

parts.note: a lot means many

explanation.surface: Someone sings another's praises but won't give the workers a pay increase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rise' is the British word for a pay increase, which the surface leans on.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to praise highly and with enthusiasm, to laud someone.

clue.text: Rebuff is short and blunt

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a cold refusal or slight
second meaning: describing a stubby turned-up nose

explanation.walkthrough: 'Short and blunt' sounds like a curt manner, fitting the rebuff, but it describes the shape of a nose.
explanation.definitionFit: A snub is a deliberate slight, and a snub nose is one that is short and turned up.

clue.text: Commons group going to the country for fun

definitions.text: going to the country for fun
definitions.note: a phrase describing the event rather than a noun

parts.note: the House of Commons is called the House
a party is a group of people

explanation.surface: A parliamentary faction goes off on a weekend jaunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going to the country' is the British phrase for calling a general election; here it is a weekend at a country house.
explanation.definitionFit: A house party is a social gathering of guests staying several days at a large country home.

clue.text: Stretcher made of sandalwood?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a device that stretches footwear to shape

definitions.note: a cryptic second meaning: wood for a sandal
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read whimsically: the wooden thing that goes into a sandal, a kind of shoe

explanation.surface: An ambulance litter has been built from fragrant timber.
explanation.walkthrough: Sandalwood is one scented timber, but the setter splits it into sandal and wood.
explanation.definitionFit: This shaped block is pushed into a boot or shoe to hold or stretch it to shape.

clue.text: It could give you a jab in the spine

definitions.text: It could give you a jab
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the sharp hollow point of a syringe used for injections
second meaning: a sharp prickle, like those on a hedgehog or a cactus

explanation.walkthrough: 'A jab in the spine' sounds like one medical injection into the backbone; split it, and spine is a prickle.
explanation.definitionFit: A hypodermic delivers injections, and the sharp prickles of a cactus or porcupine are also called by this name.
